presentingComplaint: Fever, productive cough, and worsening breathlessness for 3 days, now confused and drowsy.
history: 68-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension brought by family with a 3-day history of high-grade fever with rigors, productive cough with rusty-yellow sputum, and rapidly worsening breathlessness. Over the last 12 hours he has become increasingly drowsy and confused, not recognizing his son. No prior antibiotics or hospitalization in the last 90 days. No known TB contact. Non-smoker. No vomiting or diarrhea.
examination: Toxic-looking, drowsy, oriented only to person, GCS 13/15. Using accessory muscles of respiration. Right-sided coarse crepitations and bronchial breath sounds over the right lower and mid zones with dullness to percussion. No peripheral edema. Cool peripheries with delayed capillary refill; extremities mottled.
imaging: Chest X-ray: dense right lower and mid zone consolidation with air bronchograms; small right pleural effusion
Bilateral patchy infiltrates suggestive of multilobar involvement
microbiology: Blood cultures sent x2 sets before antibiotics
Sputum Gram stain: gram-positive diplococci, plentiful pus cells
differentialDiagnoses: Severe community-acquired pneumonia with septic shock
Acute exacerbation of heart failure (excluded — no prior cardiac history, focal consolidation)
Pulmonary tuberculosis (excluded — acute onset, no chronicity)
finalDiagnosis: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (CURB-65 4-5) with septic shock, requiring ICU admission
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Pneumonia
stewardship: Empirical combination therapy for severe CAP per IDSA/ATS 2019: a beta-lactam (e.g., ceftriaxone or ampicillin-sulbactam) PLUS either a macrolide (e.g., azithromycin) or a respiratory fluoroquinolone (e.g., levofloxacin); add MRSA/Pseudomonas coverage only if risk factors present. Concurrent early sepsis bundle care (fluids, vasopressors, source control) per Surviving Sepsis Campaign.
contraindications: Avoid fluoroquinolone monotherapy if concern for TB not yet excluded
Adjust renally-cleared antibiotic doses for acute kidney injury
Caution with fluid resuscitation given age and possible cardiac reserve — reassess with dynamic measures
edgeCases: Distinguishing severe CAP from early HAP/aspiration pneumonia is clinical — confirmed community onset here excludes HAP/VAP
Hyponatremia and thrombocytopenia may also raise suspicion for Legionella — antigen testing sent
If patient fails to improve in 48-72h, reassess for empyema, resistant organism, or alternate diagnosis (e.g., PE, ARDS)
expectedMaiK: MaiK should flag this as severe CAP meeting ICU-level severity criteria (CURB-65 high, hypotension, hypoxia, multilobar infiltrates, altered sensorium) and recommend combination empirical therapy plus early sepsis bundle, not standard ward-based monotherapy.
